result:
There is a specific, quiet magic found in the liminal spaces of the world. We are always rushing toward our destinations, obsessed with the tangible endpoints of our journeys. Yet, I have always believed that the actual destination is merely an excuse for the transit. 

Consider the soft, neon hum of an airport terminal at three in the morning. Strangers from entirely different timelines sleep sitting upright, united only by a shared, transient insomnia. Or think of the hypnotic blur of pine trees and telephone poles seen through the grimy glass of a moving train. These are the in-between zones, the geographical pauses where time seemingly bends. You are no longer who you were yesterday, but you are not yet whoever you will be tomorrow. 

In these suspended moments, the heavy obligations of real life temporarily evaporate. You are nameless, completely untethered from routine. You cannot do the laundry, clean the dishes, or answer emails while suspended thirty thousand feet above an ocean or racing through a dark tunnel. You are simply existing in the gentle hum of the engine.

We so often view travel as a mere nuisance to be endured, a desperate dash to reach a predefined location. But if you look closely, there is a profound peace hidden inside the waiting. It is a rare, modern invitation to just sit quietly and watch the ever-shifting world rush by.
